slides.hook: Customer: "And if I upgrade mid-month, what happens to the bill?" A 200-character split puts the agent's answer in the next chunk.
inside: Where a size split leaves the answer behind
Why chunk_size and overlap only move the cut
Exchange chunks with speaker and time on top
Long replies: the question on every piece

slides.title: One [exchange] / per chunk
slides.text: A call, meeting or interview is a list of speaker turns. Questions get answered in the turns after them, so chunk by exchange:

steps: Parse each turn: timestamp, speaker, text.
Start a chunk at each new question and add the replies that follow.
Fold short turns ("OK.", "Great, thanks.") into the exchange around them.
Put a header on top: call title and time span.
A reply over the size limit: split at sentences, repeat the question and the speaker label on each piece.

slides.title: Group turns into / [exchanges]
slides.text: A new exchange starts when the customer speaks after a reply. Trailing turns join the last exchange:

slides.title: The exchange / [chunker]
slides.text: One chunk per exchange, with a header. Over the limit, the question goes on every piece:

visuals.code:
def chunk(text, title, asker, max_chars=300):
    out = []
    for ex in exchanges(text, asker):
        span = f"{ex[0][0]}-{ex[-1][0]}"
        head = f"{title} · {span}"
        lines = [f"[{t}] {w}: {s}"
                 for t, w, s in ex]
        whole = "\n".join([head, *lines])
        if len(whole) <= max_chars:
            out.append(whole); continue
        qs = [l for l, x in zip(lines, ex)
              if x[1] == asker]
        for t, w, s in ex:
            if w == asker: continue
            lab = f"[{t}] {w}:"
            top = "\n".join([head, *qs, lab])
            room = max_chars - len(top) - 1
            for p in pack(s, room):
                out.append(f"{top} {p}")
    return out

cards.title: Use it when
items: Text is turns: support calls, meetings, interviews, chat logs
Questions ask what was said or agreed on a call
Answers must point to a time in the recording

cards.title: Move on when
items: No speaker labels: run speaker diarization first
One person talks for an hour (a lecture): split by topic
Questions cover the whole call: a summary per call

slides.title: [Cheat] sheet
rows: One question and its replies per chunk
Keep the speaker label and timestamp on every turn
Header on top: call title and time span
Fold "OK." and "Thanks" into the nearby exchange
Long reply: split at sentences, repeat the question and speaker
Store start and end times as metadata
Re-tuning chunk_size or overlap moves the cut to other turns

slides.line: Exchange chunks carry their call title on top. A chunk cut from a long report can say "the company" without saying which. Contextual retrieval adds a short, chunk-specific context before embedding.
